results.corrected_title: Rødt's data-centre fast-track request lacks a majority in the Storting after Frp opposes it
results.corrected_summary: According to Digi/NTB on 2 November, Rødt's request for urgent handling of stricter data-centre regulation lacked a majority for Tuesday 3 November because Frp opposed it. Frp wants all proposals handled thoroughly in the energy and environment committee. Rødt will submit a new fast-track proposal, which could be voted on the following Tuesday at the earliest. Digitalisation minister Torgeir Micaelsen said the government will act quickly but carefully and has not set specific measures or a timeline.
key_facts: Digi/NTB report published 2 Nov 2026; the request was due for consideration on Tuesday 3 Nov.
The request lacked a majority because Frp opposed it.
Rødt will submit a new urgent proposal, with a vote the following Tuesday at the earliest.
SV, MDG, KrF, Sp and Rødt want a temporary halt to new data centres.
The government wants tighter control but has decided no measures. Minister Torgeir Micaelsen said 'quickly but carefully'.
results.issues: Article from 2 Nov says request lacks a majority ahead of Tuesday; 'rejected' slightly premature. Use 'lacks a majority'.

results.corrected_title: Anthropic launches Personal Finance beta for Claude in the US
results.corrected_summary: On 5 November 2026 Anthropic announced a beta of Personal Finance for Claude. It is available to US Pro, Max and Ultra subscribers. Users connect bank and credit card accounts through Plaid, and Claude can analyse up to two years of transaction history. Conversations in the hub are not used for model training, and there are no ads or sponsored recommendations.
key_facts: Announced Thursday 5 Nov 2026, as a beta rolling out that week.
US Pro, Max and Ultra subscribers only.
Accounts are connected via Plaid. Claude can access up to two years of transactions, plus balances, credit limits and the last four digits of accounts.
Personal Finance conversations are not used to train Anthropic's models.

results.corrected_title: China's NDRC says it will accelerate comprehensive AI legislation
results.corrected_summary: At a news conference on 3 November 2026, Wang Ruomeng, a deputy director in the NDRC's Department of Innovation and High-Tech Development, said China will accelerate work on comprehensive AI legislation. The aim is foundational legislation covering the core pillars of an AI legal and regulatory system, including data, computing power, algorithms and key applications. This is a plan, not an enacted law, and no deadline was found.
key_facts: Remarks made 3 Nov 2026; Caixin published on 4 Nov.
Speaker: Wang Ruomeng, deputy director of the NDRC's Department of Innovation and High-Tech Development.
China has no unified national AI law yet.
No legislative text or deadline has been announced.
results.issues: Chatbot-dependence measures and safety-risk disclosure/incident reporting NOT confirmed as part of Wang's remarks; do not include them.

results.corrected_title: Google brings Guided Learning to Classroom worldwide and pilots it in Search for US students
results.corrected_summary: In a 3 November 2026 post, Google said Guided Learning is now available worldwide in Google Classroom, where teachers assign it as a study tool tied to class material. A pilot in Google Search for student accounts starts later in November at select US schools. AI access, including Gemini, for K-12 student accounts will be off by default until administrators turn it on.
key_facts: Guided Learning in Google Classroom is available globally.
Search pilot for student accounts starts later in November at select US schools.
AI access for K-12 student accounts (Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, Search) is off by default until admins enable it.
results.issues: Timing of default change not fixed.
